# Aunt Jamesina

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- **Status:** Widow  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Aunt Jimsie  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>; Aunty  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Jamesina is a tiny, old woman with a softly-triangular face, pink cheeks, and large, soft blue eyes filled with youth and hope. She has snow-white hair which she wears in quaint puffs over her ears. She dresses in an old-fashioned style.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052)_

## Personality

Aunt Jamesina has a youthful, mirthful, and light-hearted spirit despite her age. She possesses a very cheerful philosophy, is candid, and enjoys a good laugh, even at her own expense. She is extremely tolerant, allowing the young women she lives with to do as they please rather than trying to strictly supervise them. She has a deep affection for cats and is very fond of her friends and family.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P63](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0063), [v3 c16 P69](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0069), [v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001), [v3 c19 P39](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0039)_

- Cheerful and youthful  <sub>[v3 c16 P52](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0052), [v3 c19 P1](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0001)</sub>

## Abilities

- Knitting  <sub>[v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c19 P0](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0000)</sub>

## Goals

- To keep house for the college girls at Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000)</sub>

## History

Aunt Jamesina agreed to move to Kingsport to keep house for her niece, Stella Maynard, and her college friends Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, and Philippa Gordon at Patty's Place. She brought along her two cats, Joseph and the Sarah-cat, and eventually adopted Rusty as well. She presided over the household with humor and indulgence, refusing to strictly discipline the girls and instead letting them manage themselves. After the girls graduated, she decided to stay at Patty's Place with her cats instead of traveling or visiting relatives, remaining there to keep the house warm until they returned or moved on.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P55](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0055), [v3 c16 P59](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0059), [v3 c18 P1](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0001), [v3 c25 P10](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0010)_

## Background by volume

- Named Jamesina after her father, James, who was drowned at sea a month before she was born  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Had a daughter named Elizabeth who married and went to the foreign mission field in India  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013), [v3 c18 P25](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0025), [v3 c36 P11](../source/v03-c36.md#nw-v03-c36-p0011)</sub>
- Formerly lived in a large house before moving to Patty's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- Was once in love with a man named Milton Edwards, whom she did not marry  <sub>[v3 c35 P25](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0025)</sub>

## Quotes

> I know you expect me to look after you and keep you proper, but I'm not going to do it. You're old enough to know how to behave if you're ever going to be. So, as far as I am concerned, you can all go to destruction in your own way.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> Do your duty by God and your neighbor and yourself, and have a good time. That's my philosophy and it's always worked pretty well.  <sub>[v3 c19 P3](../source/v03-c19.md#nw-v03-c19-p0003)</sub>

> When you get rheumatism in your soul you might as well go and pick out your coffin.  <sub>[v3 c25 P10](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0010)</sub>

> You've been four of the dearest, sweetest, goodest girls that ever went together through college.  <sub>[v3 c37 P13](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0013)</sub>

> The sum and substance is that you can learn—if you've got natural gumption enough—in four years at college what it would take about twenty years of living to teach you.  <sub>[v3 c37 P24](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0024)</sub>
